title: portaBaltica article
description: The unit of publication. Every article, regardless of tier, carries a provenance record and a validator verdict. An article without a passing verdict is never served.

tier.description: A = original data journalism, B = verbatim official press release, C = link-out card. Decided by the source registry, never by the model.

status.description: Tier A goes draft -> published automatically once the validator passes. Tier B and C pass through pending_approval inside the pipeline, then the AI editor approves, rejects or escalates.

section.description: Matches the existing dashboard sections so an article can link to its live tile.

headline.description: For tier B and C this is the outlet's own headline, reproduced whole. The ceiling was 140, which is a reasonable length for a headline we write and an arbitrary one to impose on a headline we quote: the ingester truncated to fit and the verbatim check then compared our cut against their original, so every syndicated headline longer than 140 characters was rejected. Truncating another outlet's headline is itself the rewrite that rewrite_allowed: false forbids.

dek.description: Standfirst. One sentence explaining why this matters.

body.description: Structured blocks rather than a prose blob, so the validator can check numeric claims per block and the renderer can place charts inline.

chart_ref.description: Indicator id resolving to a live /data tile.

figures.description: Every numeric value appearing in this block, with the signal field it came from. The validator cross-checks these against the source payload.

rendered_as.description: How it appears in the text, e.g. '4.2%'.

persona.description: Absent on tier B and C, which carry no byline because we did not write them.

byline.description: Rendered byline. MUST contain 'AI correspondent'. Enforced by persona_rules.py, not by convention.

syndicated.description: Tier B and C only. The verbatim material and where it came from.

snippet.description: TIER C: copied verbatim from the outlet's own RSS <description>. Never rewritten, never drawn from the article body or content:encoded.

full_text.description: TIER B only, where the licence explicitly permits verbatim reproduction.

snippet_is_verbatim.description: Asserted by the ingester and re-checked by the validator against the stored raw feed item. A false value fails the build.

provenance.description: The 'паспорт материала' from the research note, made machine-readable. Rendered on the page, not just stored.

signal_id.description: The deterministic signal that triggered this story.

signal_finding.description: metric|geography|period — the reading itself, which ranking suppresses on next run so the wire does not retell a story it has already told.

cites.description: Slugs of published articles this piece drew figures from. Written by the weekly wrap, which is the only format that quotes work other than its own. It is what makes the piece correctable: a wrap outlives its citations, so retracting a cited article must be able to find every wrap that rests on it.

comparison_basis.description: What the finding is measured against, in the detector's own words.

attempts.description: How many drafts this took. A rising average means the prompt, not the model, needs work.

rejection.description: Why a rejected draft was refused, on the artifact itself. Establishing what was killing the wire once required parsing 200 blobs, because a rejected draft recorded that it failed and nothing about what failed.

model.description: e.g. gpt-4o-mini@2024-07-18. Null for tier B and C, which involve no generation.

revision.description: The git revision of the deployed code that produced this article, supplied by the deploy rather than committed to the tree. Present only when genuinely known; see revision_unavailable.

revision_unavailable.description: Why the producing revision could not be identified. Mutually exclusive with revision, so a reader can never mistake a placeholder for an answer.

research.description: Registered web sources consulted between signal detection and writing. Research supplies context, never verified figures.

documents_fetched.description: Official statements whose full page text was retrieved and read. Only ever non-zero for sources the registry marks document_fetch_allowed, which it refuses on anything but a primary official source.

document_chars.description: How much of this source's own page was read. The text itself is not copied here — it belongs to the publisher and the article links to it.

discovered_by.description: The search provider that surfaced this link, when it did not arrive in a subscribed feed. Absent means the newsroom was already subscribed.

context.description: Other series the newsroom had already retrieved that bear on this finding. Every figure here was merged into the signal payload and faces the same figures_traceable check as the detector's own.

observations.description: Deterministic statements computed from the series by code, not by a model.

analysis.description: The specialist desk's brief. Every mechanism names the verified fields that license it; ones that named nothing were deleted in code before the writer saw them, and mechanisms_discarded counts those.

revision.description: The git revision of the deployed code that produced this article, supplied by the deploy rather than committed to the tree. Present only when genuinely known; see revision_unavailable.

revision_unavailable.description: Why the producing revision could not be identified. Mutually exclusive with revision, so a reader can never mistake a placeholder for an answer.

approved_by.description: Set for tier B and C after Telegram approval.

editor.description: The desk's decision. For tier B and C this is the syndication editor; for tier A it is the review desk that reads original reporting after the validator has passed it. A judgement layer on top of the validator, never a bypass.

revision.description: The git revision of the deployed code that produced this article, supplied by the deploy rather than committed to the tree. Present only when genuinely known; see revision_unavailable.

revision_unavailable.description: Why the producing revision could not be identified. Mutually exclusive with revision, so a reader can never mistake a placeholder for an answer.

revisions.description: How many times the desk sent this piece back before deciding.

notes.description: What the desk asked the writer to change.

validator.description: The gate. An article is servable only when passed is true.

corrections.description: Append-only. Surfaced publicly on the article and in the corrections log.

then.description: Original journalism must have a disclosed byline and a body.
We did not write these, so no correspondent may claim them.
